title: CDL Hazmat marking practice questions
description: Free CDL hazmat marking practice questions on 49 CFR 172 Subpart D. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Under 172.300, when must a carrier that transports a hazardous material mark the packages, freight containers and transport vehicles?

options.A: Only when the shipper asks the carrier in writing
options.B: When Subpart D assigns the function to the carrier
options.C: Never; only the consignee may mark them
options.D: Only when the shipment crosses a state line

questions.explanation: 172.300(b): "When assigned the function by this subpart, each carrier that transports a hazardous material shall mark each package, freight container, and transport vehicle containing the hazardous material in the manner required by this subpart."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.300, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A package still bears a hazardous material's proper shipping name but holds no hazardous material or residue. Which situation does 172.303(b)(1) exclude from the prohibited-marking rule?

options.A: The package travels less than 100 miles
options.B: The driver notes the old marking on the shipping paper
options.C: The package is not visible during transportation in a transport vehicle and is loaded by the shipper and unloaded by the shipper or consignee
options.D: The package weighs less than 30 kg (66 pounds)

questions.explanation: The rule does not apply to "Transportation of a package in a transport vehicle or freight container if the package is not visible during transportation and is loaded by the shipper and unloaded by the shipper or consignee."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.303, Prohibited marking (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A trailer holds only one hazardous material (not Class 1 or Class 7) in non-bulk packages, all with the same proper shipping name and ID number, loaded at one facility, with no other cargo. What aggregate gross weight makes 172.301(a)(3) require the ID number on each side and each end?

options.A: 4,000 kg (8,820 pounds) or more
options.B: 454 kg (1,001 pounds) or more
options.C: 2,268 kg (5,000 pounds) or more
options.D: Any quantity

questions.explanation: One of the conditions is: "The aggregate gross weight of the hazardous material is 4,000 kg (8,820 pounds) or more".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.301, General marking requirements for non-bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which material does 172.301(a)(3) leave out of its rule that a vehicle carrying a large quantity of a single hazardous material in non-bulk packages be marked with the ID number?

options.A: Class 3 flammable liquids
options.B: Class 8 corrosive materials
options.C: Class 7 radioactive materials
options.D: Division 2.2 non-flammable gases

questions.explanation: "The identification number marking requirement of this paragraph (a)(3) does not apply to Class 1, Class 7, or to non-bulk packagings for which identification numbers are not required."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.301, General marking requirements for non-bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When does 172.301(d) excuse a non-bulk hazmat package from being marked with the name and address of the consignor or consignee?

options.A: When it is moved by highway and handed from one motor carrier to another
options.B: When it travels by rail in a mixed carload from several consignors
options.C: When it rides in any placarded vehicle
options.D: When it is transported by highway only and will not be transferred from one motor carrier to another

questions.explanation: The marking is required "except when the package is— (1) Transported by highway only and will not be transferred from one motor carrier to another".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.301, General marking requirements for non-bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which non-bulk package does 172.312(c) exclude from the package orientation (upright arrows) marking rule?

options.A: A non-bulk package with inner packagings which are cylinders
options.B: A single packaging fitted with vents
options.C: An open cryogenic receptacle for refrigerated liquefied gases
options.D: A combination package with 5 L inner jugs of corrosive liquid

questions.explanation: The orientation requirements "do not apply to— (1) A non-bulk package with inner packagings which are cylinders."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.312, Liquid hazardous materials in non-bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A non-bulk package holds a hazardous substance whose proper shipping name does not name that substance. What does 172.324 require on the package?

options.A: Only the reportable quantity in pounds, next to the closure
options.B: The name of the hazardous substance in parentheses with the proper shipping name, and the letters RQ with the proper shipping name
options.C: The words HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCE on every side
options.D: The EPA identification number of the shipper

questions.explanation: "The name of the hazardous substance must be marked on the package, in parentheses, in association with the proper shipping name", and "The letters “RQ” must be marked on the package in association with the proper shipping name."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.324, Hazardous substances in non-bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.302(d), which is one condition under which an emptied bulk packaging that was marked with a proper shipping name or ID number no longer has to remain marked?

options.A: As soon as it is unloaded at the consignee
options.B: When it is returned to the shipper's yard
options.C: When the driver records it as empty on the shipping paper
options.D: When it is sufficiently cleaned of residue and purged of vapors to remove any potential hazard

questions.explanation: It "must remain marked when it is emptied unless it is— (1) Sufficiently cleaned of residue and purged of vapors to remove any potential hazard; or (2) Refilled" with a material whose residue is then no longer hazardous.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.302, General marking requirements for bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A bulk packaging contains molten sulfur. How does 172.325 say it must be marked?

options.A: MOLTEN SULFUR, in the same manner as the HOT marking
options.B: HOT on the rear end only
options.C: ELEVATED TEMPERATURE on every side
options.D: Only with the shipper's name and address

questions.explanation: "Bulk packagings containing molten aluminum or molten sulfur must be marked “MOLTEN ALUMINUM” or “MOLTEN SULFUR”, respectively, in the same manner as prescribed in paragraph (a) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.325, Elevated temperature materials (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Portable tanks, IBCs and other bulk packagings
questions.question: A portable tank of hazardous material is loaded in a trailer so that its ID numbers cannot be seen from some sides. Under 172.326(c)(2), who must give the motor carrier the ID numbers for those sides of the trailer?

options.A: The consignee, on arrival
options.B: The tank manufacturer
options.C: The person who offers the portable tank to the motor carrier
options.D: The driver, who must paint them on by hand

questions.explanation: "Each person who offers a portable tank containing a hazardous material to a motor carrier ... shall provide the motor carrier with the required identification numbers on placards, orange panels, or the white square-on-point configuration" for each side and end where the tank's numbers are not visible.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.326, Portable tanks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.328(a)(1), when must a person offering a hazardous material to a motor carrier for a cargo tank give the identification numbers on placards (or affix orange panels), if the tank is not already marked?

options.A: Within 24 hours after the tank leaves the facility
options.B: Prior to or at the time the material is offered for transportation
options.C: At the first stop after loading
options.D: Before the empty return trip

questions.explanation: The offeror "shall provide the motor carrier the identification numbers on placards or shall affix orange panels containing the required identification numbers, prior to or at the time the material is offered for transportation."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.328, Cargo tanks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A cargo tank (not a nurse tank) transports a Class 2 gas. What does 172.328(b) require it to be marked with on each side and each end?

options.A: The shipper's name and address
options.B: The date of the tank's last test
options.C: The word GAS and the hazard class number
options.D: The proper shipping name of the gas or an appropriate common name for the material

questions.explanation: Each such cargo tank "must be marked, in lettering no less than 50 mm (2.0 inches), on each side and each end with— (1) The proper shipping name specified for the gas in the § 172.101 table; or (2) An appropriate common name for the material (e.g., “Refrigerant Gas”)."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.328, Cargo tanks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A cargo tank contains only gasoline. Under the table in 172.336(c), what alternative lets it go without identification numbers?

options.A: The tank is marked "Gasoline" on each side and rear in letters no less than 50 mm (2 inches) high, or is placarded under 172.542(c)
options.B: The driver carries a shipping paper that lists gasoline
options.C: The tank holds less than 3,785 L (1,000 gallons)
options.D: The tank shows the shipper's name on each side

questions.explanation: For cargo tanks that contain only gasoline, the alternative is: "The tank is marked “Gasoline” on each side and rear in letters no less than 50 mm (2 inches) high or is placarded in accordance with § 172.542(c)."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.336, Identification numbers; special provisions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: On which placard does 172.334(a) prohibit displaying an identification number?

options.A: A placard for the material's primary hazard class
options.B: Any placard on a cargo tank
options.C: A DANGEROUS placard
options.D: Any placard used on a rail car

questions.explanation: "No person may display an identification number on a RADIOACTIVE, EXPLOSIVES 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 or 1.6, DANGEROUS, or subsidiary hazard placard."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.334, Identification numbers; prohibited display (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: How does 172.336(b) treat an identification number shown on a white square-on-point display configuration?

options.A: It counts as the placard for the material
options.B: It replaces the shipping paper
options.C: It may be used only on rail cars
options.D: It is not considered to be a placard

questions.explanation: "An identification number displayed on a white square-on-point display configuration is not considered to be a placard."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.336, Identification numbers; special provisions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: During a trip, more than one of the required identification number displays on a vehicle are lost or damaged. What does 172.338 provide?

options.A: The shipper must replace them before the vehicle moves, and hand entry is not allowed
options.B: The carrier must replace them as soon as practicable, and the correct numbers may be entered by hand, legibly, with indelible marking material
options.C: The consignee replaces them on arrival
options.D: The vehicle may finish the trip without them if the shipping paper shows the numbers

questions.explanation: "The carrier shall replace all the missing or damaged identification numbers as soon as practicable. However, in such a case, the numbers may be entered by hand ... providing the correct identification numbers are entered legibly using an indelible marking material."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.338, Replacement of identification numbers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A trailer must show one ID number under 172.313(c) for materials poisonous by inhalation in non-bulk packages, and it carries one Hazard Zone A material and one Hazard Zone B material. Whose ID number is shown?

options.A: The Hazard Zone A material's
options.B: The material with the greatest aggregate gross weight, whatever its zone
options.C: The Hazard Zone B material's
options.D: Neither; the trailer shows the word INHALATION HAZARD instead

questions.explanation: When more than one such material is aboard, it is marked "For different materials in both Hazard Zones A and B, with the identification number for the Hazard Zone A material."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.313, Poisonous hazardous materials (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When does 172.313(a) say the "Inhalation Hazard" marking is not required on a package of a material poisonous by inhalation?

options.A: When the package is a bulk packaging
options.B: When it moves by private motor carrier
options.C: When the package weighs under 30 kg (66 pounds)
options.D: When the words "Inhalation Hazard" appear on the label or placard

questions.explanation: "When the words “Inhalation Hazard” appear on the label ... or placard ... the “Inhalation Hazard” marking is not required on the package."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.313, Poisonous hazardous materials (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Limited quantity and marine pollutant marks
questions.question: A package shows the limited quantity marking and is offered by highway. Under 172.315(a), when is it still subject to the 172.301 marking requirements?

options.A: When it rides on a private motor carrier
options.B: When it weighs more than 30 kg (66 pounds)
options.C: When it also contains a hazardous substance or a hazardous waste
options.D: When it is loaded in a closed van

questions.explanation: "A package displaying this mark is not subject to the marking requirements of § 172.301 of this subpart unless the limited quantity package also contains a hazardous substance or a hazardous waste."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.315, Limited quantities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Limited quantity and marine pollutant marks
questions.question: A truck carries a portable tank that is marked with the MARINE POLLUTANT mark. Under 172.322(c), how may the truck's own marking requirement be met?

options.A: By a note on the shipping paper
options.B: By the marking displayed on the portable tank loaded on the motor vehicle
options.C: By the driver telling the consignee
options.D: By one mark on the cab roof

questions.explanation: The mark must appear on each side and each end of the vehicle, and "This requirement may be met by the marking displayed on a freight container or portable tank loaded on a motor vehicle or rail car."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.322, Marine pollutants (as of Nov 4, 2026)
